neighbours.label: ' just' in the focus construction 'not just' (not just X but also Y), as against 'just' meaning recently, fair or exactly and 'not only'
fire: The festival is not just a concert but a week of workshops and talks.
Good teachers explain not just the answer but the reasons behind it.
This recipe works with any fruit, not just apples and pears.
The storm damaged not just the roofs but the power lines as well.
She wants a career, not just a job that pays the rent.
The museum is for everyone, not just students of history.
Exercise helps the mind, not just the heart and the lungs.
The new law affects not just drivers but cyclists too.
quiet: The festival is not only a concert but a week of workshops and talks.
Good teachers have just explained the answer to the whole class.
This recipe needs exactly two apples and one pear.
The storm had just damaged the roofs when the power went out.
She wants a fair and just reward for the work she did.
The museum opened just after nine on Saturday morning.
Exercise is just what the doctor ordered for his heart.
The new law affects drivers as well as cyclists in the city.
